name: Balranald-Buronga 220 kV X3 Line Trip
summary: A severe storm cell passing perpendicular to the Balranald-Buronga 220 kV X3 line resulted in the failure of six transmission towers approximately 1.6 km west of Balranald. Auto-reclosure was unsuccessful, resulting in a three-phase fault and lockout. Approximately 20 MW of generation and 3.4 MW of load at Balranald was disconnected.
source: AEMO Power System Operating Incident Report - Three-phase fault on Balranald-Buronga 220 kV X3 line on 19 January 2026

timeline.event: Severe storm cell passes perpendicular to Balranald-Buronga 220 kV X3 line
Six transmission towers fail approximately 1.6 km west of Balranald due to storm damage
Balranald-Buronga 220 kV X3 line trips on Phase B to ground fault
Auto-reclosure attempted at Buronga end - unsuccessful due to failed towers
Three-phase fault occurs during unsuccessful auto-reclosure. Voltages drop to 0.77 p.u. at Buronga across all three phases
Line trips again and locks out. Protection operated as designed
Balranald-Darlington Point 220 kV X5 line trips due to Balranald fast voltage control scheme
Approximately 20 MW of generation and 3.4 MW of Balranald load disconnected
Transgrid advises X5 line trip was due to fast voltage control scheme operation (next day)
Supply to Balranald restored via alternative supply path (3.5 hours after incident)

aemoNameMapping.description: Mapping between AEMO element names and Geoscience Australia dataset names
aemoNameMapping.notes: GA uses 'A to B' format while AEMO uses 'A – B' format. Substation names match exactly. Line circuit identifiers (X3, X5) are not in GA data - GA shows only the route, not individual circuits.

notes: This was a reviewable operating incident as the three-phase fault was a non-credible contingency event with no successful auto-reclose. The line was returned to service using temporary structures on 3 February 2026.
